record.summary: Japan's AI Safety Institute (J-AISI), launched on 14 February 2024 with its secretariat in IPA and designated in the Integrated Innovation Strategy 2024 as the central institution for AI safety in Japan. A government-related organisation in which 12 ministries and agencies and five related bodies take part, it examines and promotes evaluation methods and standards for AI safety, studies AI test environments, supports the government with research and standards, acts as a hub for industry and academia, and cooperates with counterpart institutes such as those of the UK and US.
record.notes: Announced by Prime Minister Kishida at the AI Strategy Council on 21 Dec 2023 and launched on 14 Feb 2024, with its secretariat in IPA, which falls under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and the Digital Agency. Government policy on AI safety is discussed in a liaison council of the ministries concerned with the Cabinet Office as secretariat, and project policy in the AISI Steering Committee chaired by the Executive Director. Executive Director is Akiko Murakami (part-time). The AISI Partnership Agreement with national research institutes took effect in August 2024. The second AI Basic Plan (14 Jul 2026) calls for strengthening AISI's technical evaluation and feeding its results into policy. AISI has no specific statutory basis in the AI Promotion Act.

verification.note: Stored and read: the AISI 'About' page in Japanese and AISI's Japanese and English overview decks dated 1 July 2026 (aisi.go.jp). They confirm the announcement on 21 Dec 2023, the launch on 14 Feb 2024, the designation as central institution under the Integrated Innovation Strategy 2024, the secretariat in IPA, the mandate, the governance structure and the leadership. The English deck names IPA inconsistently; the register uses the name in the site footer. The IPA press release of 14 Feb 2024 (secondary URL) returns HTTP 404 and is not stored. The statements on the second AI Basic Plan and on the AI Promotion Act are not in JP-01's stored files; no reorganisation of AISI appears in them.
